answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed if peers catch it attesting contradictory work — a mirror check where two conflicting attestations from one key prove fraud. New identities start at the nadir of trust, earning weight only through a long verifiable history of useful work, so spinning up thousands of fresh accounts buys almost nothing. The stake turns cheap identity creation into an umber-dark gamble: an attacker must risk real value on every fake, and one proven lie burns the whole deposit.
